keyword: what is the mission of artemis 2

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed test flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "10-day mission" (R1); "10 days long" (R3); "10-day mission" (R4, R5, R6); "Nearly 10 days" (R7); first crewed test flight throughout
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly describe Artemis II as a 10-day crewed test flight.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is designed to fly four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts toward space... around the moon but not land there" (R1); "Four astronauts on the Artemis II mission are on their way to journey around the moon" (R3); "flying four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the moon" (R4); "four astronauts... circle Earth and the moon" (R5); "send four astronauts on a looping journey around the moon" (R6); "four-person crew... fly around the Moon" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts flying around the Moon and back without landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first human mission to lunar orbit since 1972.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "around the moon but not land there"; "swing around, passing over the far side" (R1); "lunar flyby" (R4, R6); no mention of entering lunar orbit, described as flyby/free-return trajectory
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe a flyby trajectory around the Moon, not entering lunar orbit; Apollo 17 (1972) involved orbit and landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis II's primary mission is to validate NASA’s deep-space systems including life support, navigation, and the SLS rocket before future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey and keep its crew alive" (R1); "confirm all of the spacecraft's systems operate as designed... life support... Guidance, navigation, and communications" (R6); "testing all of its life-support, navigation, and other systems" (R7); SLS launch referenced throughout
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state validation of deep-space systems like life support, navigation, and SLS for future landings.

verifications.claim: Artemis II's mission includes pioneering research on human health in deep space.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: CubeSats "measure the effects of space radiation on human beings" (R1); "ARCHeR will monitor... well-being... AVATAR... impacts of radiation and microgravity on human health... changes to the immune system" (R3); "exercise equipment... effects of microgravity on the human body" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention health-related experiments (radiation, microgravity, immune), but describe as tests/demonstrations rather than explicitly 'pioneering research'.

verifications.claim: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen" (R1); same crew listed (R3-R7)
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names match across all sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission will fly around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "passing over the far side" (R1); "swing around the moon's far side" (R3); "loops around the far side of the moon" (R4); "venture beyond the far side of the Moon" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm flyby around the far side.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission includes the furthest travel from Earth of approx. 252,799 miles in human history.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "252,799 miles, or 4,144 miles farther than the Apollo 13 astronauts" (R1); "travel a maximum distance from Earth of 252,799 statute miles — besting the Apollo 13 record" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Exact distance and record-breaking claim directly supported.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew will test the Orion spacecraft's life support.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "checking out the key systems aboard Orion, including life support" (R1); "systems checks" incl. life support (R4); "testing out the Orion capsule’s... air quality control system" (R5); "test life-support" (R6); "life-support" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention testing life support systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew will test the Orion spacecraft's communications.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "deep-space communications" checks (R1); "standard operations like communications" (R4); "life-support systems work... deep-space communications" (R5); "communications systems" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of testing communications in deep space.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew will test the Orion spacecraft's maneuvering capabilities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "manually flew the spacecraft, nudging it close... mimicked the maneuvers" (R1); "manual close‑range maneuvering" (R2); "proximity operations... demonstrate Orion's ability to fly in tandem" (R4)

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew will perform a 70-minute manual test-drive of the capsule in space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "approximately 70‑minute activity... manual close‑range maneuvering" (R2); "proximity operations, or 'prox ops'" described as manual flying (R4)

verifications.claim: Artemis II uses a free return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "free return trajectory" (R1, R3); "free-return trajectory" (R4); "hybrid free-return trajectory" (R6)

verifications.claim: Artemis II's free return trajectory ensures the Moon’s gravity will slingshot the spacecraft back to Earth without needing engine maneuvers if a propulsion failure occurs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "free return trajectory. This path uses the moon’s gravity to swing the capsule directly back to Earth without needing to fire any of its engines... even if there were a failure of the propulsion system" (R1); "slingshot 'free return' trajectory... even if its engines never fired again" (R3); "free-return trajectory — a course that loops around... returns to Earth using gravity, even in the event of major system failures" (R4)

verifications.claim: Artemis II flight is scheduled to conclude with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R1-R7 all confirm Pacific splashdown)

verifications.claim: Artemis II follows the successful uncrewed Artemis I flight in 2022
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Following the success of the Artemis I uncrewed test flight in 2022" (R7); "Artemis 1... in 2022" (R1, R4, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis II follows successful uncrewed Artemis I in 2022.
